easy: A big feeling of wonder when you see something amazing.

ex.en: We stared at the huge waterfall in awe.
ex.ko: 우리는 경이로운 마음으로 거대한 폭포를 바라보았다.

easy: A deep feeling of respect for someone or something very great.

ex.en: The students felt awe when they met the famous astronaut.
ex.ko: 학생들은 유명한 우주비행사를 만나고 깊은 경외감을 느꼈다.

easy: A rule that says something is not allowed.

ex.en: The banning of phones in class started on Monday.
ex.ko: 교실에서 휴대폰을 금지하는 규칙이 월요일부터 시작되었다.

easy: Soldiers who fight while riding horses.

ex.en: The cavalry rode across the field on fast horses.
ex.ko: 기병대는 빠른 말을 타고 들판을 가로질러 달렸다.

easy: A box where a person who has died is placed.

ex.en: The old coffin in the museum was made of stone.
ex.ko: 박물관에 있는 오래된 관은 돌로 만들어져 있었다.

easy: Having lots of bright colors.

ex.en: The colorful kite flew high above the beach.
ex.ko: 알록달록한 연이 해변 위로 높이 날았다.

easy: Full of exciting and interesting things.

ex.en: Grandpa told us colorful stories about his life.
ex.ko: 할아버지는 자신의 삶에 대한 다채로운 이야기를 들려주셨다.

easy: To stand up against someone who is against you.

ex.en: The goalie had to confront the other team's best player.
ex.ko: 골키퍼는 상대 팀 최고의 선수와 맞서야 했다.

easy: To face a hard problem and not run away from it.

ex.en: I had to confront my fear and jump into the pool.
ex.ko: 나는 두려움에 맞서 수영장에 뛰어들어야 했다.

easy: Able to decide who wins or what happens in the end.

ex.en: Her last goal was the decisive point of the game.
ex.ko: 그녀의 마지막 골이 경기의 결정적인 순간이었다.

easy: Very clear, so nobody can doubt it.

ex.en: Our team had a decisive lead at the end of the race.
ex.ko: 우리 팀은 경주가 끝날 때 확실하게 앞서 있었다.

easy: Made to look nice, not to be used for a job.

ex.en: The decorative pillows on the sofa are just for looks.
ex.ko: 소파 위의 장식용 쿠션은 보기 좋으라고 놓은 것이다.

easy: Known as the best and most trusted of its kind.

ex.en: This is the definitive book about dinosaurs.
ex.ko: 이것은 공룡에 관한 결정판 책이다.

easy: To slowly change and grow into something new over a long time.

ex.en: Birds evolved from small animals long ago.
ex.ko: 새는 아주 오래전에 작은 동물에서 진화했다.

easy: To make something blow apart with a big bang.

ex.en: The workers exploded the big rock to make a road.
ex.ko: 일꾼들은 길을 내려고 큰 바위를 폭파했다.

easy: The shape and style of the letters you see on a page or screen.

ex.en: I picked a big, fun font for my school poster.
ex.ko: 나는 학교 포스터에 크고 재미있는 글꼴을 골랐다.

easy: A swimming race where you can swim any way you like.

ex.en: My sister won the freestyle race at the pool.
ex.ko: 누나는 수영장에서 열린 자유형 경기에서 우승했다.

easy: To stick one thing to another with something sticky.

ex.en: I glued the paper stars onto the card.
ex.ko: 나는 종이 별을 카드에 풀로 붙였다.

easy: Covered with a lot of hair.

ex.en: Our hairy dog needs a bath every week.
ex.ko: 우리 털이 북슬북슬한 강아지는 매주 목욕을 해야 한다.

easy: A short way to say "that is" or "in other words."

ex.en: I like pets that bark, i.e., dogs.
ex.ko: 나는 짖는 동물, 즉 개를 좋아한다.

easy: Money or things that a person gets from family after they die.

ex.en: She got her grandmother's ring as part of her inheritance.
ex.ko: 그녀는 유산의 일부로 할머니의 반지를 받았다.

easy: Strange because the opposite of what you expected happened.

ex.en: It was ironic that the fire station caught fire.
ex.ko: 소방서에 불이 난 것은 아이러니한 일이었다.

easy: Turning from solid into liquid.

ex.en: The melting snowman became a puddle.
ex.ko: 녹고 있는 눈사람이 물웅덩이가 되었다.

easy: When heat changes something hard, like ice, into liquid.

ex.en: The melting of the ice made the river rise.
ex.ko: 얼음이 녹으면서 강물이 불어났다.

easy: A kitchen machine that heats food very fast.

ex.en: Mom warmed my soup in the microwave.
ex.ko: 엄마는 전자레인지에 내 수프를 데워 주셨다.

easy: To make something as small as possible.

ex.en: Wear a helmet to minimize the chance of getting hurt.
ex.ko: 다칠 위험을 줄이려면 헬멧을 써라.

easy: To say that something is smaller or less important than it really is.

ex.en: Don't minimize his help; he worked very hard.
ex.ko: 그의 도움을 과소평가하지 마, 그는 정말 열심히 했어.

easy: To take the outside skin off a fruit or vegetable.

ex.en: Dad peeled an orange for me.
ex.ko: 아빠가 나에게 오렌지 껍질을 까 주셨다.

easy: To come off in small, thin pieces.

ex.en: The paint on the old fence is peeling.
ex.ko: 낡은 울타리의 페인트가 벗겨지고 있다.

easy: A person who sings, plays, or acts for people watching.

ex.en: The performer on the stage played the drums.
ex.ko: 무대 위의 공연자가 드럼을 연주했다.

easy: A fun trip where you eat outside.

ex.en: Our class went on a picnic by the lake.
ex.ko: 우리 반은 호숫가로 소풍을 갔다.

easy: Something that is very easy to do.
ko: 식은 죽 먹기, 아주 쉬운 일

ex.en: The spelling test was a picnic for me.
ex.ko: 받아쓰기 시험은 나에게 식은 죽 먹기였다.

easy: Mostly; for the most part.

ex.en: The class is predominantly girls this year.
ex.ko: 올해 우리 반은 대부분 여학생이다.

easy: From the very early times, simple and not fancy.

ex.en: Early people used primitive tools made of stone.
ex.ko: 옛날 사람들은 돌로 만든 원시적인 도구를 썼다.

easy: A scientist who studies how people think and feel.

ex.en: The psychologist talked with kids about feelings.
ex.ko: 심리학자는 아이들과 감정에 대해 이야기를 나누었다.

easy: Able to make babies or new living things.

ex.en: Flowers are the reproductive part of a plant.
ex.ko: 꽃은 식물의 번식을 맡는 부분이다.

easy: To limit what people can do.

ex.en: The school will restrict phone use during class.
ex.ko: 학교는 수업 중 휴대폰 사용을 제한할 것이다.

easy: Quiet and shy, and not showing off.

ex.en: The retiring new girl sat quietly in the corner.
ex.ko: 수줍음 많은 전학생은 구석에 조용히 앉아 있었다.

easy: About to leave a job after working there for many years.

ex.en: Our retiring principal waved goodbye to everyone.
ex.ko: 퇴임하는 우리 교장 선생님이 모두에게 손을 흔들어 작별 인사를 했다.

easy: When people or teams try hard to beat each other.

ex.en: There is a friendly rivalry between our two schools.
ex.ko: 우리 두 학교 사이에는 우호적인 경쟁이 있다.

easy: Money paid to a writer or artist when people use their work.

ex.en: The author gets royalties every time her book sells.
ex.ko: 그 작가는 책이 팔릴 때마다 인세를 받는다.

easy: Kings, queens, and their families.

ex.en: Royalty lived in the big castle on the hill.
ex.ko: 왕족은 언덕 위의 큰 성에 살았다.

easy: A tube of ground meat, often cooked for breakfast.

ex.en: I ate a sausage and eggs for breakfast.
ex.ko: 나는 아침으로 소시지와 달걀을 먹었다.

easy: To grab something quickly and hold it tight.

ex.en: The cat seized the toy mouse with its paws.
ex.ko: 고양이는 앞발로 장난감 쥐를 꽉 움켜잡았다.

easy: To take something by force.

ex.en: The soldiers seized the castle in the night.
ex.ko: 군인들은 밤에 그 성을 점령했다.

easy: Tasting hot and burning in your mouth.

ex.en: This spicy soup made my tongue tingle.
ex.ko: 이 매운 국물 때문에 혀가 얼얼했다.

easy: Able to stick to things like glue.

ex.en: My fingers got sticky from the candy.
ex.ko: 사탕 때문에 내 손가락이 끈적끈적해졌다.

easy: Wet and clingy from sweat.

ex.en: I felt sticky after playing soccer in the heat.
ex.ko: 더운 날 축구를 하고 나서 몸이 끈적끈적했다.

easy: A sudden, sharp pain, like from a bee.

ex.en: I felt the sting of the cold wind on my face.
ex.ko: 차가운 바람이 얼굴을 따끔하게 쳤다.

easy: Enough; as much as is needed.

ex.en: The soup was sufficiently hot for me.
ex.ko: 수프는 내가 먹기에 충분히 뜨거웠다.

easy: In a way that shows you are grateful.

ex.en: She thankfully took the gift from her friend.
ex.ko: 그녀는 친구의 선물을 고마운 마음으로 받았다.

easy: A word you use when you are glad something turned out well.

ex.en: Thankfully, the rain stopped before our game.
ex.ko: 다행히 경기 전에 비가 그쳤다.

easy: A short, sharp sound, like a clock makes.

ex.en: I could hear the tick of the clock in the quiet room.
ex.ko: 조용한 방에서 시계의 째깍 소리가 들렸다.

easy: A tiny bug that bites animals and people to drink their blood.

ex.en: We found a tick on our dog after the hike.
ex.ko: 하이킹을 다녀온 뒤 우리 강아지에게서 진드기를 발견했다.

easy: Coming right after nineteenth.

ex.en: I finished twentieth in the long race.
ex.ko: 나는 장거리 달리기에서 스무 번째로 들어왔다.

easy: Not nice; making you feel bad or uncomfortable.

ex.en: The garbage had an unpleasant smell.
ex.ko: 쓰레기에서 불쾌한 냄새가 났다.

easy: Having no link to something else.

ex.en: His question was unrelated to our math lesson.
ex.ko: 그의 질문은 우리 수학 수업과 관련이 없었다.

easy: Not part of the same family.

ex.en: The two boys look alike but are unrelated.
ex.ko: 그 두 남자아이는 닮았지만 친척 사이는 아니다.

easy: Empty, with nobody in it.

ex.en: There was one vacant seat on the bus.
ex.ko: 버스에 빈 자리가 하나 있었다.

easy: Showing no thought, like staring without really seeing.

ex.en: He had a vacant look on his face during the boring talk.
ex.ko: 지루한 이야기를 듣는 동안 그의 얼굴은 멍했다.

easy: A small opening that lets air or gas out.

ex.en: Warm air blew out of the vent in the floor.
ex.ko: 바닥의 통풍구에서 따뜻한 바람이 나왔다.

easy: Looking pale and weak.

ex.en: The sick boy looked wan and tired.
ex.ko: 아픈 남자아이는 창백하고 피곤해 보였다.

easy: Turning and curving, not going straight.

ex.en: We followed a wandering path through the woods.
ex.ko: 우리는 숲속의 구불구불한 길을 따라갔다.

easy: All the clothes a person has.

ex.en: Her wardrobe is full of bright dresses.
ex.ko: 그녀의 옷장에는 화려한 드레스가 가득하다.

easy: The good feeling you get when something is warm.

ex.en: I felt the warmth of the fire on my hands.
ex.ko: 나는 손에 모닥불의 온기를 느꼈다.

easy: A kind, loving feeling toward others.

ex.en: Grandma greeted us with warmth and a big hug.
ex.ko: 할머니는 따뜻한 마음으로 우리를 꼭 안아 맞아 주셨다.

easy: To chop something with an axe.

ex.en: Dad axed the logs for our campfire.
ex.ko: 아빠는 캠프파이어를 위해 통나무를 도끼로 패셨다.

easy: To stop something for good.

ex.en: The school decided to ax the old rule.
ex.ko: 학교는 그 오래된 규칙을 없애기로 했다.

easy: The prettiest girl at a party or dance.

ex.en: She was the belle of the school dance.
ex.ko: 그녀는 학교 댄스파티의 인기 있는 미인이었다.

easy: A short news report or notice.

ex.en: The school bulletin said there is no class on Friday.
ex.ko: 학교 공고에 금요일에는 수업이 없다고 적혀 있었다.

easy: To work together with others for the same goal.

ex.en: The kids cooperate to build a big sand castle.
ex.ko: 아이들은 큰 모래성을 쌓으려고 협력한다.

easy: A person whose job is to give advice about problems.

ex.en: The school counselor helped me when I felt sad.
ex.ko: 학교 상담 선생님은 내가 슬플 때 도와주셨다.

easy: A grown-up or teen who looks after kids at summer camp.

ex.en: Our camp counselor taught us how to paddle a canoe.
ex.ko: 우리 캠프 지도 교사는 카누 젓는 법을 알려 주셨다.

easy: The stone edge where the sidewalk meets the street.

ex.en: Wait on the curb before you cross the street.
ex.ko: 길을 건너기 전에 인도 가장자리에서 기다려라.

easy: Meant by fate to happen or to become something.

ex.en: The hero was destined to save the kingdom.
ex.ko: 그 영웅은 왕국을 구할 운명이었다.

easy: Calm and not caught up in feelings.

ex.en: He seemed detached and did not care about the game.
ex.ko: 그는 초연해 보였고 경기에 관심이 없는 듯했다.

easy: To spread something out to many places or people.

ex.en: Farmers distribute seeds across the field.
ex.ko: 농부들은 씨앗을 밭 곳곳에 뿌린다.

easy: Money used in the country of Vietnam.

ex.en: He paid for the noodles with Vietnamese dong.
ex.ko: 그는 베트남 돈인 동으로 국수 값을 냈다.

easy: To make a ringing sound like a big bell.

ex.en: The church bell dongs every hour.
ex.ko: 교회 종이 한 시간마다 댕댕 울린다.

easy: In a way that uses little time or effort and works well.

ex.en: The new machine washes dishes efficiently.
ex.ko: 새 기계는 설거지를 효율적으로 한다.

easy: Kind words that show you like what someone is doing.

ex.en: My coach's encouragement made me try again.
ex.ko: 코치 선생님의 격려 덕분에 나는 다시 도전했다.

easy: Something that gives someone hope and makes them feel braver.

ex.en: Her cheers gave me a boost of encouragement.
ex.ko: 그녀의 응원이 나에게 힘이 되었다.

easy: Covered with water.

ex.en: The flooded street was full of puddles.
ex.ko: 물에 잠긴 거리는 물웅덩이로 가득했다.

easy: Doing something risky when you cannot be sure it will work out.

ex.en: Going out in the storm was a big gamble.
ex.ko: 폭풍 속에 나가는 것은 큰 모험이었다.

easy: The player who guards the goal in soccer or hockey.

ex.en: The goalkeeper jumped and caught the ball.
ex.ko: 골키퍼가 뛰어올라 공을 잡았다.

easy: Not able to hurt anyone.

ex.en: The garden snake is harmless.
ex.ko: 정원에 사는 뱀은 해롭지 않다.

easy: A person who comes from Hungary.

ex.en: My friend is a Hungarian who loves soccer.
ex.ko: 내 친구는 축구를 좋아하는 헝가리 사람이다.

easy: The language that people speak in Hungary.

ex.en: She speaks Hungarian with her grandparents.
ex.ko: 그녀는 조부모님과 헝가리어로 이야기한다.

easy: Not real; only in your mind.

ex.en: My little brother has an imaginary friend.
ex.ko: 내 동생에게는 상상 속의 친구가 있다.

easy: Locked up and not free to leave.

ex.en: The imprisoned bird flapped against the cage.
ex.ko: 갇힌 새가 새장에 부딪히며 퍼덕였다.

easy: Not staying the same; changing from time to time.

ex.en: Her rules are inconsistent, so we never know what to do.
ex.ko: 그녀의 규칙은 일관성이 없어서 우리는 어떻게 해야 할지 모른다.

easy: A school for young kids before first grade.

ex.en: My little brother starts kindergarten this fall.
ex.ko: 내 동생은 올가을에 유치원에 들어간다.

easy: A person from a country in Latin America.

ex.en: My neighbor is a Latino who plays the guitar.
ex.ko: 우리 이웃은 기타를 치는 라틴아메리카 사람이다.

easy: In a way that makes a lot of sound.

ex.en: The crowd cheered loudly for our team.
ex.ko: 관중은 우리 팀을 큰 소리로 응원했다.

easy: A person who fixes cars.

ex.en: The mechanic changed the tire on our car.
ex.ko: 정비사가 우리 차의 타이어를 갈아 주었다.

easy: To make something softer or less strong.

ex.en: The teacher agreed to modify the rule for younger kids.
ex.ko: 선생님은 어린 학생들을 위해 규칙을 완화하기로 했다.

easy: Not taking care or paying attention.

ex.en: Neglect of the plants made them dry up.
ex.ko: 식물을 돌보지 않아서 말라 버렸다.

easy: A place left alone and not cared for.

ex.en: The old barn fell apart from years of neglect.
ex.ko: 오래된 헛간은 수년간 방치되어 무너졌다.

easy: Toward or in the northwest.

ex.en: We drove to the northwestern edge of the park.
ex.ko: 우리는 공원의 북서쪽 끝까지 차를 몰고 갔다.

easy: Being cruel and unfair to people and not letting them be free.

ex.en: The people fought against the king's oppression.
ex.ko: 사람들은 왕의 억압에 맞서 싸웠다.

easy: Loving your country.

ex.en: The patriotic crowd waved flags on the holiday.
ex.ko: 애국심 가득한 사람들이 기념일에 깃발을 흔들었다.

easy: The baseball player who throws the ball to the batter.

ex.en: Our pitcher threw a fast ball.
ex.ko: 우리 투수는 빠른 공을 던졌다.

easy: A jug with a handle and a spout for pouring drinks.

ex.en: Mom poured lemonade from the pitcher.
ex.ko: 엄마는 주전자에서 레모네이드를 따라 주셨다.

easy: An outdoor place where kids play.

ex.en: We played on the swings at the playground.
ex.ko: 우리는 놀이터에서 그네를 탔다.

easy: Having people living there.

ex.en: This island is populated by only a few families.
ex.ko: 이 섬에는 몇 가정만 살고 있다.

easy: Likely to be true or to happen, but not for sure.

ex.en: Rain is probable tomorrow, so bring an umbrella.
ex.ko: 내일은 비가 올 가능성이 높으니 우산을 가져가라.

easy: A short time when a new worker is tested to see if they fit the job.

ex.en: The new cook is on probation for one month.
ex.ko: 새 요리사는 한 달 동안 수습 기간 중이다.

easy: A guess about the future based on what happened before.

ex.en: The projection says our town will have more kids next year.
ex.ko: 예상에 따르면 내년에는 우리 동네에 아이들이 더 늘어날 것이다.

easy: Showing a picture from a film on a screen.

ex.en: The projection of the movie started at noon.
ex.ko: 영화 상영은 정오에 시작되었다.

easy: A part of the body, like an eye or ear, that senses things.

ex.en: The nose is a receptor that lets us smell.
ex.ko: 코는 냄새를 맡게 해 주는 감각 기관이다.

easy: A new version of something that was made before.

ex.en: I liked the remake of that old cartoon.
ex.ko: 나는 그 옛날 만화의 리메이크작이 마음에 들었다.

easy: To make something again in a new way.

ex.en: They will remake the movie with new actors.
ex.ko: 그들은 새 배우들로 그 영화를 다시 만들 것이다.

easy: The way someone plays a song or acts a part.

ex.en: Her rendering of the song made everyone clap.
ex.ko: 그녀의 노래 연주에 모두가 박수를 쳤다.

easy: The way someone explains what something means.

ex.en: Each student gave a different rendering of the poem.
ex.ko: 학생마다 그 시를 다르게 해석했다.

easy: Making babies or new plants and animals.

ex.en: Reproduction in frogs begins with eggs in the water.
ex.ko: 개구리의 번식은 물속의 알에서 시작된다.

easy: A small sea animal with a curved body that people eat.

ex.en: We had fried shrimp for dinner.
ex.ko: 우리는 저녁으로 새우튀김을 먹었다.

easy: A man who speaks for a group or a company.

ex.en: The team's spokesman answered the questions.
ex.ko: 팀의 대변인이 질문에 답했다.

easy: Marked with dirty or colored spots.

ex.en: My shirt was stained with grape juice.
ex.ko: 내 셔츠에 포도 주스 얼룩이 졌다.

easy: A small space in a barn where one animal stays.

ex.en: The horse stayed in its stall at night.
ex.ko: 말은 밤에 자기 마구간 칸에서 지냈다.

easy: Very hungry because there is not enough food.

ex.en: The starving puppy ate the food very fast.
ex.ko: 굶주린 강아지는 먹이를 아주 빨리 먹었다.

easy: A long, thin band used to tie things or hold them.

ex.en: The strap on my backpack broke.
ex.ko: 내 배낭의 끈이 끊어졌다.

easy: A loop on a bus or train that you hold so you do not fall.

ex.en: I held the strap while the train moved.
ex.ko: 나는 기차가 움직이는 동안 손잡이 고리를 잡았다.

easy: Based on your own feelings, not on facts.

ex.en: Which song is best is a subjective opinion.
ex.ko: 어떤 노래가 가장 좋은지는 주관적인 의견이다.
